messages:
Alex (oncall): seeing a sudden spike of 502/504s from hosted inference in us-east-1, started ~08:23 UTC. multiple CS tickets.
Priya - CS: 12 customers reported timeouts, some long streaming sessions dropped. customers complaining about retries and duplicate billing calls.
Samir (infra): looking at ingress, auth-proxy error rate jumped at 08:22. p50 auth latency 40ms -> p95 2.4s then 5xxs started.
DevOps: getting logs now, one pattern: token refresh calls flooded /auth/validate with identical payloads (no jitter)
CS-Bot: created incident IA-4312 and linked tickets [T-785, T-786] :spiral_notepad:
Alex (oncall): can we throttle at the gateway to avoid cascade?
Nadia (platform): temporarily enabling link-level circuit breaker and 5s auth timeout for host-level route, deploying in 30s.
Samir (infra): adding observability: auth_proxy.request_id and client_id tagging so we can correlate tenant spikes.
DevOps: rolling change now -> applied to front fleet. watch p50/p95 for 5xx.
Alex (oncall): quick repro snippet from affected client (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "rwd-large",
  "stream": true,
  "prompt": "<long-prompt>"
}
```
Samir (infra): backend logs show auth validation errors like: `ERROR auth_proxy: upstream 502 invalid_token` but upstream auth service returned 200 for some requests. I suspect connection reuse/keepalive hitting a buggy proxy path.
DevOps: workaround: disable keepalive reuse on the auth proxy pool and add small jitter to refresh. deploying now.
Priya - CS: started CS comms draft to impacted customers: offering 10% credit for last 24h and ETA for fix.
Nadia (platform): temporary fallback route configured to a lower-cap stateless model variant for streaming-heavy tenants — reduces auth calls frequency because it accepts shorter-lived session tokens.
Alex (oncall): telemetry after mitigations: 5xx rate down 78% in 7m, streaming drop rate reduced. good sign.
Samir (infra): root cause hypothesis: internal token heartbeat process had deterministic schedule (no jitter) causing thundering refresh across clients after TTL change yesterday. auth-proxy kept connections alive and sometimes forwarded stale connections -> 502s.
DevOps: short-term action items we did: disable keepalive on auth pool, add jitter to client-side heartbeat, circuit-break auth path, add fallback routing.
Nadia (platform): postmortem action items (to track):
- enforce jittered token refresh in SDKs and runtimes (owner: SDK team)
- harden auth-proxy connection handling and add retry with backoff (owner: infra)
- add synthetic streaming-scenario canary that exercises auth refresh patterns (owner: sdet)
- per-tenant rate-limits at edge for auth validations to avoid single tenant blast radius (owner: platform)
- review billing double-charge detection window and auto-credit rules (owner: finance/CS)
Priya - CS: CS follow-up: send final comms after 24h and verify credits applied.
Alex (oncall): follow-up checklist for next 48h: verify canary is green, monitor p95 auth latency, and confirm SDK patch release.
Samir (infra): I'll open infra-1298 with logs and repro steps + test harness for auth-proxy keepalive case. attaching minimal repro script in issue.
DevOps: timeline: mitigation deployed 08:26, fallback routing 08:28, full SDK rollout for jitter by EOD tomorrow.
Priya - CS: closing loop with customers for those who responded, collecting any remaining traces.
CS-Bot: incident IA-4312 marked 'mitigated' at 08:30 UTC, will remain open for postmortem and action items. :white_check_mark:
Alex (oncall): thanks team. we'll run a brief postmortem doc tomorrow with timeline and action owners.
